description: wt - git worktree helper for PowerShell: pick, cd, add, check out, rename, remove and clean worktrees, Claude Code's included.
post_install: # The registry PSModulePath was just extended; this process still has the old value.
$mods = if (Get-Command modulesdir -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) { modulesdir $global } else { Join-Path (Split-Path (Split-Path (Split-Path $dir))) 'modules' }
# Set up 'git wt': a global git alias to git-wt.ps1 in $dir, the 'current' junction, so updates keep it
# valid. The module writes it (one tested place). The profile is left alone: 'git wt install profile'
# adds the wt command for those who want it, and a profile line from an older install keeps working.
post_uninstall: # Drop the 'git wt' alias if post_install set it (an update runs this, then sets it again).
if ((git config --global --get alias.wt) -match '/apps/psworktree/current/git-wt\.ps1') { git config --global --unset alias.wt }

if ((Test-Path $profilePath) -and (Select-String -Path $profilePath -Pattern 'Import-Module\s+PSWorktree\b' -Quiet)) { Write-Host "Gone for good? The 'Import-Module PSWorktree' line in $profilePath can go too - harmless until then (-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)." }
notes: 'git wt' works now, from any shell (a global git alias). Type 'git wt help' to start.
git runs an alias in a child process, so 'git wt' prints the path where it would cd. For cd, add the
wt command to your PowerShell profile: git wt install profile - or, in Git Bash: git wt install bash
